title: Element boundary handling preserves neighboring markup

context.hint: Review parser boundaries for a filter that removes disallowed active content while preserving permitted markup.
context.surface: A standalone HTML filter handles element boundaries, comments, quoted attributes, and URL-valued fields in static documents.
assumptions: The filter contract defines which elements and attributes are allowed and how permitted content is preserved.
The source evidence covers focused local fixtures. Integrated and browser-level verification remain open.

review.invariant: Element policy follows the tokenizer's boundaries. Surrounding allowed text and inert comments are preserved according to the filter contract.
review.verification: Use inert fixtures to check removal of a disallowed element, handling of an incomplete element, and exact preservation of neighboring allowed text and comments. Include a document consisting entirely of permitted markup.

source_observation.summary: Six local fixtures passed after a draft boundary correction. The fixtures covered element boundaries, incomplete markup and benign round trips. Combined filter behavior and the benchmark verifier remained untested in this run.
